clue.text: King known for complex work about eastern princess

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for work goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work
Di is the usual crossword princess, Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A monarch is famous for an elaborate project concerning a princess from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like an adjective for the work, but it belongs to the definition: the Freudian complex is named after this king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theban king of Greek myth gave his name to Freud's complex about a son's desire for his mother.

clue.text: Overhead expense East German soldier absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed means taken in, so the soldier goes inside the German word

parts.note: Ost is German for east
NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier from East Germany soaked up the overheads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' reads as a nationality, but it is the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: An oncost is a business overhead, a cost not tied to a particular product.

clue.text: Plunder communication system in new lido

indicators.note: in places the system inside the scrambled letters
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is telepathic communication

explanation.surface: Looters raid the phone network at a newly built swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'communication system' suggests phones, but it is telepathy, extrasensory perception. 'new' shuffles the pool to DOIL, and the telepathy abbreviation goes 'in' after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to strip of valuables by force, which is to plunder.

clue.text: Health worker came with a drip prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A nurse arrived with an intravenous drip ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is an emergency medical worker who treats patients before hospital.

clue.text: Tacked in all directions

parts.note: S is South, one of the four compass points
E is East, one of the four compass points
W is West, one of the four compass points
N is North, one of the four compass points

explanation.surface: A boat zigzagged every which way across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacked' suggests sailing to and fro, which the directions support, but it means loosely stitched. The four compass points are taken in the order South, East, West, North.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking is sewing with long temporary stitches, so something tacked has been stitched.

clue.text: A big blow for everyone when they're close!

definitions.text: A big blow for everyone when they're close!

parts.words: A big blow for everyone when they're close!
parts.note: on a weather map, lines of equal pressure packed close together mean strong winds for all

explanation.walkthrough: 'they' are lines on a weather chart; 'close' means near each other, and 'blow' is a gale, not a punch or a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: These lines join points of equal atmospheric pressure, and when tightly spaced they signal high winds.

clue.text: Twist together in sleepy port, arresting onset of tedium?

indicators.note: arresting means holding in custody, so the first letter is held inside

parts.note: inert means sluggish or sleepy

indicators.note: onset of means the beginning, the first letter of the word

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A sleepy harbour town stops boredom from setting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour but is the drink. T goes into INERT after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: To intertwine is to twist or wind things around each other.

clue.text: Additional top removed from dam

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: An extra layer is taken off the top of a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' suggests a river barrier, but it is a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean further or extra, as in 'other duties', so it means additional.

clue.text: Weapon, a chap said, holds up animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are taken for their sound

parts.note: a guy is a chap

explanation.surface: A man describes a weapon propping up an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a guy', spoken, gives the ending AGAI; 'holds up' puts ASS above it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai, or assegai, is a slender spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Swell engulfing bomber oddly put under water

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the letters go inside the swell

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A rising sea swallows a bomber, which oddly ends up underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: To submerge something is to plunge it beneath the surface of water.

clue.text: Races we organised —— long, like this one?

definitions.text: Races we organised —— long, like this one?

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the races they set up ran long, perhaps like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: this race at Newmarket is a long-distance handicap, over two and a quarter miles, so 'long, like this one' describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cesarewitch is a long-distance flat horse race, a handicap run each autumn at Newmarket in England.

clue.text: Eg sister's mistake, ditching husband on retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
ditching means throwing away, so the letter for husband is removed

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: A sister's error, made after leaving her husband once she has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British for a mistake; without H it is BIS, which 'on retirement' turns back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sib is a sibling, a brother or sister, so a sister is one example.

clue.text: Boisterous male taken in by lie

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the letter for male goes within the word for lie

parts.note: a story is a falsehood, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: A rowdy man is fooled by a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy can describe noisy, turbulent behaviour, just as boisterous does.

clue.text: Suspend introduction, changing sides nearly halfway through

indicators.note: the sides are left and right, so the L just short of the middle of the word swaps to R

parts.note: a prologue is an introduction to a play or book

explanation.surface: An instruction to put off a preface, swapping sides partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' are L and R (left and right); the L is the fourth of eight letters, nearly halfway.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue parliament is to suspend its sittings without dissolving it.

clue.text: Politician (female, not male) on Spanish cape

indicators.note: female, not male tells us to put F where M stood

parts.note: a minister is a government politician
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A woman politician stands on a Spanish headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Finisterre is a rocky headland on the coast of Galicia in north-west Spain.

clue.text: Royal attendant's son staying with one in Scotland

parts.note: a lad is a boy or son
yin is the Scots word for one
waiting means staying put

explanation.surface: A courtier's boy is lingering with someone north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'attendant' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; the pieces go in the order LAD, YIN, WAITING.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady-in-waiting is a noblewoman who serves a queen or princess as a personal companion.

clue.text: Failure of equilibrium breaks main cable

indicators.note: breaks means smashes apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loss of balance snaps the main cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' reads as the verb of the sentence, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbalance is a lack of balance, a failure of stability or equilibrium.

clue.text: Austere master takes a lot of flak, keeping in cricket side

indicators.note: keeping in means holding inside, so the side goes within the master's letters

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree holder, who takes on the next piece
on is the leg side of a cricket field

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to give someone stick is to criticise them, flak

explanation.surface: A stern teacher gets heavy criticism while staying on the cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs; STICK, short of K, gives STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic means like monks' life, which is simple and austere.

clue.text: Distasteful thing European accepts on bail, perhaps

parts.note: an object is a thing

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An unpleasant item: a European agrees to release on bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' joins the pieces, with E taking the scrambled ONBAIL (IONABL) in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something objectionable is offensive or unpleasant, so it is distasteful.

clue.text: At start of month traveller climbs tree

parts.note: Jun is the abbreviation for June
the start of a month is its first day, the 1st, written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: Early in the month, a traveller scales a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At start of month' reads as a date, the first of June: JUN with I for 1. 'climbs' turns REP upward into PER.
explanation.definitionFit: The juniper is an evergreen coniferous tree or shrub whose berries flavour gin.

clue.text: Refined English member introducing a book

indicators.note: introducing means coming before, placing the limb ahead of the rest

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A cultured English club member presents a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests someone in a club, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish, which is refined.

clue.text: Show up and apply one's mind

definitions.meaning: to be present at an event, to turn up
to pay attention or give heed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both being present at something and paying attention to something.

clue.text: Disown senior officer returning in a bad temper

indicators.note: in places the turned officer inside the other pieces

parts.note: bate is an old British word for a rage or fit of temper

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the officer's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: GEN is the abbreviation for General

explanation.surface: A general, in a fury, rejects a senior officer on his return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns GEN into NEG, which goes into A BATE; BATE is a dated British word for a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or reject, which is to disown.

clue.text: Diver in meagre beachwear

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words meagre beachwear

explanation.surface: A swimmer in a skimpy bathing costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' suggests a person, but it is a bird that dives.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a water bird that dives underwater for fish.

clue.text: A chain bridge in London

definitions.meaning: a watch chain worn across a waistcoat
a road bridge across the Thames between Chelsea and Battersea

explanation.surface: A suspension bridge in the capital, held up by chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses take the name of Queen Victoria's consort: a waistcoat watch chain and a Thames crossing in Chelsea.

clue.text: Stylish greeting framed by county council

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the greeting goes between the council letters

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for county council
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A fashionable welcome is surrounded by local government.
explanation.walkthrough: A county council is the local government of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means fashionably elegant, which is stylish.

clue.text: Warning: this place is a dump

definitions.meaning: in Britain a rubbish dump is often called by this short word

explanation.surface: A sign warns visitors that the site is used for dumping rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this place is a dump' is also what people say of a messy room, which in Britain is called this word too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a piece of advice or warning and a British rubbish dump.

clue.text: Such vessels need attention, note, in rough weather

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to give them attention

indicators.note: in places the note inside the scrambled letters
rough suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Boats need care and a written reminder in stormy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships, but they are pots. 'rough' shuffles the weather into THEWARE, and the note goes 'in' after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthenware is pottery made of baked clay, so pots and jugs are such vessels.

clue.text: Procession demanding my time, say, and energy

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
eg (for example) is signalled by say
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A parade that takes up a lot of someone's time and strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation 'my!', as in surprise, giving COR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a solemn procession, especially of mourners at a funeral.

clue.text: Head of Charterhouse took a break -like 22,perhaps

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: rested means took a break

explanation.surface: The headmaster of Charterhouse school paused, like the diver bird perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headmaster of Charterhouse, an English public school, but it takes only the C. The definition points to 22, the grebe: the great crested grebe has a head plume.
explanation.definitionFit: The great crested grebe carries a crest of feathers on its head, so a grebe may be described as tufted.
